description:
Fetch a single live URL on demand (plain HTTP GET, no JavaScript) and return its parsed SEO elements, clean markdown content and optionally raw HTML — so you can inspect any page mid-conversation without launching a crawl. Always returns a `fetch` block (final_url, status_code, redirect_chain, content_type, response_time_ms, page_size_bytes (decoded/uncompressed size), fetched_at). `include` selects extra blocks: "seo" (title, meta_description, meta_robots, x_robots_tag, canonical, hreflang, html_lang, viewport, h1/h2, og/twitter tags, json_ld_types, word_count, internal/external/nofollow link counts, images_missing_alt), "content" (main body as markdown, truncated at 100 KB) and "html" (raw HTML, truncated at 200 KB); default ["seo","content"]. Non-HTML responses return only the fetch block. On a transport failure the result carries a structured `error` (dns_error, timeout, connection_error, too_large, blocked_url, too_many_redirects) instead. http/https only; private/reserved hosts are blocked. Free; rate-limited per user.

Cost: free.

Examples:
```json
// inspect the SEO elements and content of a page
{"url":"https://seocrawl.ai","include":["seo","content"]}
```

followRedirects.description: Follow up to 5 redirects (the full chain is always reported). Default true.

include.description: Which blocks to return beyond the always-present fetch block. Default ["seo","content"].

name: fetch_url
title: Fetch a live URL
